items.proposed_content: The isometric de Branges representation converts the weighted interval problem into exact quadrature over orthogonal kernel nodes. The endpoint's position among the interlacing zeros selects the original or auxiliary node family and hence the appropriate construction; because the majorant and minorant share that quadrature and interpolate at ±β, their difference is the sharp two-delta extremizer.

items.proposed_content: A first Montgomery test supplies the known low-frequency contribution to a small-gap minorant but leaves an unknown positive tail. A separate sinc-squared test converts positivity and diagonal multiplicity into a triangular-moment lower bound for that tail; two integrations by parts then express the first test's tail through the same integrated moment, making it usable in the final pair-count bound.

items.proposed_content: Fourier support is the interface between family-specific correlation estimates and a reusable extremal layer. The general-bandwidth Beurling-Selberg calculation packages the latter by Δ, so the q-aspect correlation window through 2-ε can use the same scaled majorants and minorants with a larger Δ than the zeta window through one, producing stronger leading constants.

items.proposed_content: Point constraints form a kernel-cost hierarchy in the fixed weighted bandlimited space: enforcing the value at zero costs the reciprocal diagonal mass 1/K(0,0), while enforcing values at ±β costs 2 divided by K(β,β)+|K(β,-β)| because the two evaluations can share off-diagonal correlation. The optimal interval-sandwich width realizes exactly the latter two-point cost.
